problem: VLM-based navigation systems such as NaVILA feed a fixed window of sparsely sampled past frames as history, which gives no structured motion memory. NaVILA's own ablation shows no gain when scaling from 8 to 64 frames.
motivation: Long-horizon VLN requires knowing where the agent has been, how it turned, and which parts of the instruction are done. Raw frame history is an indirect and sparse account of motion. Hippocampal path integration compresses motion into compact episodic traces, which suggests treating trajectory as an explicit modality.
key_idea: Encode the full action and relative-pose history with a contrastively trained Bi-GRU into one embedding, project it into the frozen Qwen3-VL-8B token space, and prepend it as a single trajectory-memory token at each step.
insight: A single learned motion token carries cumulative heading information that neither text action history nor no history provides. On the Q1 heading query, BITE reaches about 0.83 while both baselines collapse to about 0.07, because they answer 'same' regardless of input. The ablation on input features shows that cumulative position and heading features (5-D and 7-D) are needed for good retrieval, whereas 2-D and 3-D local features fail. Note that the results are diagnostic probes on synthetic trajectories, not navigation benchmark performance.
method: 7-D motion features: converts discrete actions (stop/forward/left/right; step 0.25 m, turn 15°) into [cx, cy, sinθ, cosθ, Δθ, is_forward, is_turn] with cumulative position and heading.

Group-aware contrastive batching: 3600 start-goal groups with 10 augmented trajectories each (36,000 in total) built from R2R/RxR. Each batch has 6 groups (B=60), giving 9 positives and 50 negatives per anchor.
BITE encoder: 2-layer Bi-GRU (256 hidden per direction), masked mean-pool to 512-D, MLP head 512→256→128, and L2 normalization (302K parameters).
Multi-positive InfoNCE: SimCLR-style loss with temperature 0.07 over all 9 same-endpoint positives, so the embedding captures what is invariant across path variants.
Multimodal projector: 2-layer GELU MLP (128→1024→4096; the paper states W1 as 1024×256), 4.46M parameters, the only part trained during alignment while the encoder and Qwen3-VL-8B stay frozen.
Token injection: one soft token e_traj is prepended to [current view, sparse frame history, instruction] at every step, so token cost is constant regardless of trajectory length.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (frozen) + Bi-GRU trajectory encoder (trained contrastively, then frozen) + trained MLP projector
setting.training_data: 36,000 augmented trajectories (3600 start-goal groups × 10) built from R2R and RxR action/pose sequences for the encoder; projector alignment data is not clearly specified
setting.observation: current RGB camera view + sparse frame history + language instruction + action/pose history
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (stop, forward 0.25 m, turn-left/right 15°)
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (qualitative R2R episodes); quantitative probes on synthetic trajectories

numbers_note: No standard VLN benchmark results (SR/SPL/NE) are reported; the paper says R2R/RxR val-unseen evaluation is ongoing work. Only synthetic probe accuracies (Q1/Q2 on random trajectories) exist, so they are not included as benchmark numbers.
results: On probe queries over random trajectories of 20-124 steps, BITE+Qwen3-VL reaches 0.65 overall accuracy, versus 0.26 for text history and 0.21 for no history. It reaches 0.83 on the cumulative-heading query, where both baselines get about 0.07, and it matches text history on action-frequency. At 124 steps it uses 41 tokens versus 903 for text history (4.5%).
limitations: No evaluation on standard VLN benchmarks (R2R/RxR SR, SPL, NE) and no comparison to NaVILA; the paper says this is ongoing work.
Evaluation uses synthetic probe questions and only three qualitative Isaac Sim episodes; the baselines are weak, since the base model always answers 'same' on Q1.
The trajectory is dead-reckoned from ideal discrete actions (fixed 0.25 m / 15°) with no odometry noise, and the emergent 'instruction localization' claim is only qualitative.
compares_to: NaVILA (cited only for its frame-history ablation)
